rule_level_problems.problem: The page gives no possible-anaphylaxis criteria; the rule is invented. Its first four branches make any single sudden itch/rash/face or tongue swelling alone enough, and the any2 list omits abdominal pain/vomiting while including insect bite/sting. Acceptable as a broad pre-screen per the briefing but not page-traceable.
'Generalised' itch/rash is lost in both symptom branches (left ≥2-of-4 and right and-branch), so localised itch or rash counts.

The 'previously caused anaphylaxis' Yes-branch relies on an allergy record to the substance (or Insect venom for stings) rather than a link to prior anaphylaxis; any recorded allergy plus exposure triggers probable anaphylaxis without symptoms. Matches page structure but is a proxy.
The right branch (no exposure) is not conditioned on absence of exposure; harmless superset, but the left and right branches are not distinct as on the page.
Age band is 'adult' while the gold anaphylaxis page uses all_ages; confirm intended population.

summary: The probable-anaphylaxis flowchart is encoded faithfully (exposure plus allergy, >=2-of-4 via any2, and the no-exposure and-branch), the Urgent priority is tied to the Anaphylaxis diagnosis, and all five 'other allergy' rules exist with correct types. The main gaps are the lost 'generalised' qualifier on itch/rash, minor lost qualifiers (red, 24 hours, most days, both eyes), and an invented, page-untraceable possible rule. Management bullets are out of scope by design.
